title: Shop machines pay nothing per order
subtitle: A FARM shop machine gives back every charge it makes, so serving one client or seventeen earns the same. Only what is still open at the end of the shift counts. The agents' failure to serve has another cause: no arm, not even one paid by the world for each serve, ever serves an order.

blocks.title: About 0 per served order: exactly 0 on 3 of the 10 shop machines
blocks.text: On `shop-serve` every one of the 724 orders the scripted worker served on the judge's 100 test seeds netted exactly 0, as on the 2 ladder machines without a siren. On the other 7 machines a served order pays +1 or -1 on 2.2% to 7.1% of orders (siren pay falling between serves), a mean of -0.003 to -0.010. A client arriving costs 3, and taking the order, cooking and serving pay 1 each back. So the episode return only counts what is still open at the end: solve 0, take one order and stop -2, idle -3, serve one order and stop -3.

items: **The machines rank the plans right, by little.** The solve is the best plan on every machine, but only by 0.47 to 1.85 per episode discounted (0.71 on `shop-serve`), and serving more orders does not raise it.

**It is the pricing rule, not a bug and not the model.** All 10 clause sets equal the card's answer. A machine with a net-positive loop is refused at build time, and the end charge for an order left open is off by default since commit `deff802`.

**Pricing is not why the agents serve 0.** 0 of 51 trained shop runs served any order in their 100 test episodes (0%, 95% CI [0%, 7.0%]), no-RM and FARM with the world's +1 per serve included. On the six counted cards serving needs cooking, and no arm gets that far: an exploration limit of every arm.

**What made the shop learn before was an end cost.** Every shop run that learned had an open promise that cost something as the step limit ran out: 12 of 12 seeds served, against 0 of 12 with both costs off (see [Shop promise cost](../shop-promise-cost/index.html)). Even with that cost on, `shop-serve` learned 0 of 3: random play never prepared food in 1,000 episodes.

blocks.text: **Take one order, stop** runs the scripted worker until the first order is taken, then does nothing. **Serve one, stop** runs it until the first serve. **Pay per served order** sums the machine's pay from the step after one serve to the next serve, over every order the solve served; the -1 to +1 spread is a siren or a boiling pot charged or paid back between two serves. On the ladder's first two rungs no order is taken, so "take one order, stop" plays the whole solve.

Serving one order and stopping pays less than taking one order and stopping (-3 against -2 on `shop-serve`): the serve brings the next client, and that client's -3 is never paid back. The trained FARM agents' RM return of -2.00 on serve, full, quiet-first and boil (table below) is exactly this local optimum.

"Pay per extra order" is the solve's gain over serving one, divided by the extra orders: 0.04 to 0.18 discounted, so a twelfth order is worth almost nothing. sections.title: Why: the pricing rule works as designed

items: **No final state, so no completion pay.** The +10 is paid only on an edge into a final state (`app/src/compiler/reward_layer.py:643-646`); the shop machines have none.

**Progress is a potential over the stages still owed.** Without a final it aims at the states where nothing is pending (`reward_layer.py:763`, `:772`). The chain weights (`reward_layer.py:399-420`) give `Response(client_arrived, order_taken)` weight 3, since it hands off to the order and cooking rules. So an arrival charges -3 and order, cooking and serve pay back +1 each: every loop sums to 0.
**A positive loop is refused at build** (`reward_layer.py:183`). Record: `docs/decisions/arm-fm/rm-execution.md:233-236` ("It stays a potential, so no loop gains").

**Nothing charges an order still open at the end.** The end judgment is off by default (`app/src/config/config.py:269-271`, commit `deff802`), and benchmark runs set `time_limit_penalty: 0.0` (`app/src/benchmark/traces.py:39-42`), so the runtime adds nothing at the time limit (`app/src/arm_fm/runtime.py:222-226`).
**The world turns a serve into a new charge.** The next client comes a gap after the previous one is served (`app/src/arm_fm/shop.py:88-91`).

**Discounting adds only a small push.** The pay is undiscounted and the learner is not, so each step with stages open costs about (1 - gamma) times the stages owed. The switch to discounted shaping was left "to decide after the shop runs" (`docs/COMPILER_REWARD_DESIGN.md:154-163`, `rm-execution.md:271-273`).

blocks.title: A right machine for these tasks should not pay per order
blocks.text: In LTLf, `G(client_arrived -> F order_taken)` counts no orders: it holds on a finite trace when no arrival is left without its answer, so serving 1 or 17 clients is equally correct. Throughput comes from the world, not from the instruction. What a machine should do is price an order left open, which the end judgment or the promise cost does (both existing switches, both off in the final run).
